metadata.Name: Large Japanese Web Corpus
metadata.Description: A large-scale Japanese web corpus created from 21 snapshots of the Common Crawl archive (2020-2023). It was built to improve the quality of training data for Japanese LLMs, surpassing existing corpora like CC-100 and mC4 in size. The final corpus contains approximately 312.1 billion characters from 173 million pages, refined through a multi-stage filtering and deduplication process to ensure high quality.
metadata.Paper Title: Building a Large Japanese Web Corpus for Large Language Models
Affiliations: Department of Computer Science, School of Computing, Tokyo Institute of Technology
Global Scientific Information and Computing Center, Tokyo Institute of Technology
metadata.Abstract: Open Japanese large language models (LLMs) have been trained on the Japanese portions of corpora such as CC-100, mC4, and OSCAR. However, these corpora were not created for the quality of Japanese texts.nThis study builds a large Japanese web corpus by extracting and refining text from the Common Crawl archive (21 snapshots of approximately 63.4 billion pages crawled between 2020 and 2023).nThis corpus consists of approximately 312.1 billion characters (approximately 173 million pages), which is the largest of all available training corpora for Japanese LLMs, surpassing CC-100 (approximately 25.8 billion characters), mC4 (approximately 239.7 billion characters) and OSCAR 23.10 (approximately 74 billion characters).nTo confirm the quality of the corpus, we performed continual pre-training on Llama 2 7B, 13B, 70B, Mistral 7B v0.1, and Mixtral 8x7B Instruct as base LLMs and gained consistent (6.6--8.1 points) improvements on Japanese benchmark datasets.nWe also demonstrate that the improvement on Llama 2 13B brought from the presented corpus was the largest among those from other existing corpora.
